During the Fifth Quarter (covering the performance period 10/1/2022 to 12/31/2022), the team completed the Go/No-Go milestone requirement by successfully de-icing using ≥5 piezoelectric transducers and achieving an efficiency improvement of 25% over the baseline during that experiment (efficiency measured at 3,340%). Additionally, the team investigated the effectiveness of a phone motor-vibration mechanism for de- icing and found that it performs well. During the Sixth Quarter (covering performance period 1/1/2023 to 3/31/2023), the team successfully investigated mounting solutions for both the motor and piezoelectric solution to vibrational de-icing. During the motor study, the team compared two soft-mount devices with a standard fixed-mount and found that the effect on performance is minor, if any. The conclusion from this study is that soft mounts are acceptable for use with motors for this technology. During the piezoelectric study, the team conducted experiments to compare four epoxies and found that some epoxies performed better. During both the motor and piezo studies, the team achieved de- icing efficiencies exceeding 100% compared to a fully thermal process. Also, the team developed the breadboard amplifier by making key design improvements to the existing amplifier. Finally, the team soft-started the setup and testing of a full-scale heat exchanger and successfully formed significant frost on the unit. Fig 6.
